chunks: Al-Husayn ibn 'Ubayd Allah informed me, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan ibn 'Ali, from 'Amr ibn Sa'id, from Musaddiq ibn Sadaqa, from 'Ammar ibn Musa, from Abu 'Abd Allah (peace be upon him):

He said: The kafan (burial shroud) should be a burd (striped cloth). If it cannot be a burd, then make it all cotton. If you cannot find a cotton turban ('imama), then make the turban of sabiri (fine woven cloth).

key_terms.الْكَفَنُ: kafan: the burial shroud used to wrap the deceased
key_terms.بُرْدًا: burd: a striped woven garment; the most preferred material for the kafan
key_terms.سَابِرِيًّا: sabiri: a type of fine, thin woven cloth permitted for the turban when cotton is unavailable
key_terms.عِمَامَةَ: 'imama: the turban component of the kafan, wrapped around the head
key_terms.قُطْنًا: cotton (qutn): the acceptable full-kafan substitute when burd is unavailable

ai.seo_question: What material does Imam al-Sadiq (AS) prescribe for the kafan (burial shroud) in al-Istibsar, and what substitutes are permitted?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (AS), transmitted through a chain of prominent Imami scholars, establishes the preferred material for the burial kafan (shroud). A burd (striped cloth) is the ideal; if unavailable, the entire kafan should be cotton; and if a cotton turban cannot be found, fine sabiri cloth is permitted as a substitute for that component.
